subject: Logging auditability & redaction — post-discovery recap and action plan
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@novahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Wang <rachel.w@novahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: logging visibility & PII masking requirements

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — helpful overview. A few items we want captured so we can move this through security review at NovaHealth: 

- Exact controls you offer for request/response log redaction (headers, bodies, trace IDs). We need answers for automated vs. manual approaches.
- Retention windows for different log types and whether retention is configurable per-tenant.
- Guarantees around not persisting unredacted PII in any long-term storage (ingest, backup).
- Evidence we can hand to our auditors: sample audit log export, masking config snapshot, SOC2 section reference.

Can you confirm a short list of deliverables and an estimated timeline for a short PoC (1 week) where we validate: 1) request logs are masked to our spec, 2) trace IDs are obfuscated, and 3) we can route redacted logs to our Splunk instance?

Attaching the requirements sheet (redaction_req_v1) we mentioned.

Next steps from our side: security will triage and loop in procurement if the PoC looks good. We prefer to do a technical review with your infra engineer during the PoC kickoff. Any chance Mon/Tue next week for a 60-minute session?

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Product Security Engineer
NovaHealth

Attachments: redaction_req_v1.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@novahealth.com>, Rachel Wang <rachel.w@novahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: logging visibility & PII masking requirements

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap and proposed action items from our side: 

Recap of capabilities we discussed:
- Redaction layers: 1) ingest-time pattern masking (regex and named fields), 2) runtime field scrubbing (response sanitizers), 3) post-ingest transformation for archived logs.
- Trace IDs: by default we retain correlation IDs for tracing but can emit an obfuscated hash version (customer-specific salt) to any long-term logs to preserve traceability without surfaceable raw IDs.
- Retention: configurable per-tenant; default 30 days for request-level logs, 365 for aggregated metrics. Can shorten or disable long-term retention on a per-customer basis.

Deliverables we can provide for PoC (1 week):
1) A redaction configuration applied to a sandbox tenant (we will share the exact config JSON/PDF).
2) A short script to replay a subset of production-like traffic into the sandbox so you can validate masking.
3) A Splunk sink we configure (with your credentials) to push redacted logs to your index.
4) An export bundle: sample audit log + masking config snapshot + step-by-step verification checklist.

Requested engineers for kickoff: Monica (infra/runtimes) and Lauren (security & compliance). Monica — can you confirm the masking knobs and whether we need to pause KV-cache writes during the PoC? Lauren — we may need a one-pager on compliance artifacts (SOC2 sections we reference).

Proposed kickoff windows: Tue 2027-03-23 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 2027-03-24 11:00-12:00 PT. Alex / Rachel — which works for you?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redaction_requirements_matrix.xlsx (draft)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@novahealth.com>, Rachel Wang <rachel.w@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: logging visibility & PII masking requirements

All — quick technical answers inline and a few notes for the PoC.

1) Ingest-time masking: we support multiple strategies — pattern rules (regex), named field masking (configured per model/input schema), and allow-listing for headers that may carry PHI metadata. Pattern and field rules apply before any write to ephemeral disk.

2) Runtime KV/cache: we do NOT persist unredacted KV cache snapshots to long-term storage. There are ephemeral caches for response generation that are kept in memory and flushed; for the PoC I recommend we enable in-memory only mode and disable periodic cache dumps to object storage. That will remove a class of leakage.

3) Trace ID obfuscation: we offer two modes — truncate-and-hash (recommended) and tokenization via customer-provided salt. For auditability we keep an internal correlation mapping that is accessible to us under NDA; the exported logs for NovaHealth will only contain hashed IDs.

4) Log retention per-tenant: configurable via the console or API. We can set NovaHealth sandbox to 7 days during PoC and demonstrate the lifecycle policy (delete/expire).

5) Evidence bundle: I will prepare a sample audit export plus the masking config and a short verification checklist. We can include a diff showing raw->redacted examples.

PoC operational notes:
- I will need a Splunk ingestion endpoint and an API key with a test index. Please provide a secure upload (we prefer a short-lived secret in the kickoff meeting).
- For the traffic replay we will provide a sanitized dataset. If you want us to use a live replay, we will require a signed data processing addendum (DPA) first.

Action items assigned:
- Monica: produce evidence bundle + sandbox config (ETA Wed EOD 3/24).
- Lauren: produce SOC2 mapping doc for the security team (ETA Wed 3/24 morning).
- Alex / Rachel: confirm kickoff window and supply Splunk endpoint + test creds (ETA EOD 3/23).

Monica
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redaction-matrix-v1.pdf

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@novahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rachel Wang <rachel.w@novahealth.com>, NovaHealth Security <security@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Logging auditability & redaction — post-discovery recap and action plan

Thanks — that all sounds good. We can do the Tue 3/23 09:00 PT kickoff. I just shared a service account key with Monica via our secure vault and created a test Splunk index: nh_logs_test.

A few clarifications from our security team: 
- We expect the PoC logs to never contain unredacted patient identifiers. If a raw trace is ever needed for a full incident investigation, we need a clear legal/ops path and an audit trail showing who requested and accessed the raw mapping.
- Please include a one-page summary of how backups are handled and whether any historic backups might contain unredacted logs.

Procurement note: our SOW template will need a short clause on log residency and a commitment that NovaHealth's logs for production will be stored only in us-east-1. Is that something you can commit to for production? (We understand sandbox can be elsewhere for testing.)

We'll be ready to start the PoC Tuesday morning. Looking forward to the evidence bundle.

Best,
Alex
Senior Product Security Engineer — NovaHealth
